lessons.title: Only one multi-Region design is supported
lessons.why: AWS says Global Resiliency is the supported multi-Region approach, and that unsupported designs can affect quotas and the SLA story.
paras: You replicate a linked instance, put numbers in a traffic distribution group, and shift telephony and agents in 10 percent steps. Pairs are Northern Virginia and Oregon, Frankfurt and London, Tokyo and Osaka. New instances from 1 September 2026 get global routing, analytics, and contact search by default. Older ones can be migrated on request.

ReplicateInstance copies flows, modules, users, profiles, queues, hours, quick connects, and number associations. It does not copy prompts that live only as loose S3 objects in the way people assume. Read the replica page before the test.
points: Identity has to work in both Regions.
A Lambda in the flow must exist in both Regions.
Osaka delivery can take up to 20 seconds.
Shift 10 percent first. Do not start at 100.
lessons.mistake: A second unrelated instance and a DNS trick.

lessons.title: What a failover drill has to prove
lessons.why: A drill that only signs an admin in has not tested a customer call.
paras: Place a call to a number in the distribution group, confirm which Region answered, shift the percentage, and place another call. Sign an agent out and into the other Region. Open a recording and a CTR in the Region that took the call.
Then fail one dependency you added: a Lambda, a prompt, a Lex alias. The replica is only as complete as those dependencies.
points: Write the expected caller experience during the shift.
Include the IdP endpoint in the firewall test.
Measure the Osaka delay if that is your pair. Do not discover it in an incident.
Rollback is a shift back, and you should time it.
lessons.mistake: A tabletop that never moves a percentage.

lessons.title: Migration patterns that survive contact with a Monday
lessons.why: The pattern is dual-run, a small number, evidence, then the rest. Heroic cutovers are how recordings go missing.
paras: Build the flow and the queue while the old platform still owns the number. Compare a day of CTRs with a day of the old report. Port a pilot number. Watch audio, screen pop, and WFM. Then port the range, with a rollback window the carrier has agreed.
Global Resiliency is not a migration tool from CUCM. It is how the Connect instance itself survives a Region. You may need both: a bridge during the move, and a pair after it.
points: Reports will not match on day one if the old AHT included something yours does not. Write both formulas.
Agents need the CCP network before the port, not after.
Keep the old recording system until the new object's retention is proven.
One number is a test. A range is a decision.
lessons.mistake: Porting the main toll-free number as the first test.
